name: Video upload and streaming
needs: let users upload videos and play them back smoothly
my videos buffer and take forever to load
host course videos in my app
summary: Taking a video file, turning it into several sizes and qualities, and sending viewers small pieces that fit their connection. A plain MP4 link works for short clips, but long or user uploaded video needs encoding into a streaming format like HLS so it starts fast and doesn't stall.
need_when: Users upload their own videos, or you host lessons, demos or recordings.
Videos are longer than a minute or two, or people watch on phones.
Some videos should only be watched by people who paid or logged in.
skip_when: A few public marketing videos. An unlisted YouTube or Vimeo embed is free and good enough.

ways.title: Video API
ways.cost: Per minute stored and watched. Cloudflare Stream lists $5 per 1,000 minutes stored and $1 per 1,000 delivered
ways.how: Mux, Cloudflare Stream or Bunny Stream take the upload, encode it, and give you a playback ID and a player.
ways.tradeoff: Quickest to do well. Costs grow with every minute watched, and your videos live with them.

ways.title: Encode it yourself
ways.how: A background job runs ffmpeg to make HLS renditions, stores them in object storage and serves them through a CDN.
ways.tradeoff: Cheapest at scale and fully yours. Encoding is slow and heavy, and you own every playback bug.

ways.title: Embed from a video site
ways.how: Upload to YouTube or Vimeo as unlisted and embed their player.
ways.tradeoff: Free and simple. Their branding and suggestions, weak privacy, and no fit for user uploads.

prompt:
Add video upload and streaming.

Requirements:
- Use [Mux / Cloudflare Stream / ffmpeg to HLS on our own storage]. Upload from the browser straight to the provider or storage, not through my server.
- Accept [MP4, MOV, WebM] up to [2 GB] and [60 minutes]. Check type and size before the upload starts.
- Save a video record with owner, status (uploading, processing, ready, failed), duration and provider ID. Update it from the provider's webhook.
- Show a processing state, then the player when ready. Show a clear message if processing fails.
- Private videos use signed playback URLs that expire. Only the owner and people allowed by [rule] can get one.
- Deleting a video in the app deletes it from the provider or storage.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Upload a 1 GB test video from a phone on a slow connection. It finishes, and the page shows processing, then ready.
2. Play it on a phone and a laptop. Quality changes with the connection without the video stopping for long.
3. A private video's link stops working for a logged out user or after it expires.
4. Delete a video in the app. It's gone from storage and the player too, and stops counting toward storage costs.
acceptance_checks: Upload a 1 GB test video from a phone on a slow connection. It finishes, and the page shows processing, then ready.
Play it on a phone and a laptop. Quality changes with the connection without the video stopping for long.
A private video's link stops working for a logged out user or after it expires.
Delete a video in the app. It's gone from storage and the player too, and stops counting toward storage costs.
if_you_skip_it: Big uploads time out on your server, viewers on phones sit through buffering, and private videos end up on a public link anyone can share.
